mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the trigger is met, or the median return is not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household wealth and lower equity demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer and business confidence, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances, or the median return is not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) over a 6-month window indicates a rebalancing toward durable goods and future income, which typically supports higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the average return is not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals reduced household financial buffers and increased spending on equities for liquidity, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10).
